html:
Global attention is seized by escalating tensions between the US and Iran, with the US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent declaring sanctions will 'squash' Iran's economy and 'collapse' its regime, demanding allies choose sides. This comes as NPR reports on the "US war with Iran" being connected to other global conflicts, and Iran's foreign ministry condemning the new US sanctions as 'economic terrorism' and 'crimes against humanity'.

Great Power Politics: The confrontation between the US and Iran has intensified, with Trump stating no talks are planned and claiming the Strait of Hormuz as 'new US territory,' a claim swiftly rejected by Iran's Leader’s adviser and Iran negotiator Ghalibaf, who insists the strait remains under Iranian control and will not open until US demands are met. The UAE has accused Tehran of firing ballistic missiles at shipping and has suspended all trade with Iran, while a bulk carrier in the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly hit by an unknown projectile, resulting in a crew casualty. Separately, Iran is reportedly considering attacking US military targets in Europe if Trump escalates the conflict, while China is pushing back against Trump’s economic pressure on Iran, with analysts suggesting strong trade ties could hinder isolation efforts. In Eastern Europe, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko reports at least 17 people were killed in a "massive attack" overnight, as Russia 'purposefully' hit critical infrastructure, disrupting hot water supply and with attacks spilling over into Romanian and Moldovan territory. North Korea also fired suspected missiles toward the sea, shortly after Trump suggested he would meet Kim Jong Un later this year, and following the scaling back of US-South Korea military drills. Meanwhile, in China, property developer Hui Ka Yan, founder of Evergrande, has been sentenced to life in prison.

Middle East Security: The Israeli-Palestinian conflict remains a significant regional flashpoint. UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Canada have condemned Israel's 'E1' West Bank settlement project, joining Jordan and Egypt in warning of its potential to divide the West Bank. Israel's military admitted its troops fired on a car in Gaza in 2024 that killed five-year-old Hind Rajab and six family members, ordering a criminal investigation which her family has rejected. Alarmingly, Israel’s Ben-Gvir posted a video of a gallows site for hanging Palestinians, as multiple reports detailed the construction of dedicated prison wings for this purpose. Human Rights Watch noted a record year for settler attacks, which are driving Palestinian displacement, with settlers reportedly attacking over 160 water sites in the West Bank during 2026.

Global Economy and Markets: The US national debt has surpassed $40 trillion, a figure attributed to extensive borrowing and spending. In Europe, an ongoing drought is driving up transport costs and food prices, as rivers dry up and crops fail in Germany and across the continent. China's world’s top humanoid robot maker surged in its market debut, highlighting advancements in the sector.

Humanitarian and Migration Challenges: Nigeria experienced a tragic boat capsize in Sokoto state, leaving dozens dead, with many victims feared to be children. More than 1,000 Afghan refugees who aided US forces during the war have remained stuck in a camp in Qatar since 2021. The US has also deported 20 people to Liberia as part of a new agreement that could see up to 1,200 migrants sent to the West African nation under Trump’s immigration crackdown, while Spain expanded migrant shelters in Ceuta following a recent influx from Morocco.

Other Major Events: A woman has been charged with planning an Islamic State-inspired attack on the New York state capitol building. Melania Trump made a public appearance at a Rose Garden event, while the Trump administration faces renewed questions over top aide Natalie Harp's security clearance after reports she worked without it for a year. Separately, an FBI team seized devices from former US representative Eric Swalwell and raided his home in connection with sexual assault allegations. In South America, a 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck Peru's southern Andes, with tremors felt as far as Lima.
